verses.sanskrit:
वैशम्पायन उवाच।
              अनुभूय तु राज्ञस्तं राजसूयं महाक्रतुम्। युधिष्ठिरस्य नृपतेर्गान्धारीपुत्रसंयुतः॥१॥
verses.english: Vaishampayana said O king, having been impressed with the great Rajasuya sacrifice of king Yudhishthira and having also learnt the intentions of Duryodhana, from what he said, and also in order to do what was pleasing to him (Duryodhana), the son of Subala, Shakuni, accompanied by Gandhari's son (Duryodhana) to the king Dhritarashtra whose knowledge was his eye, seated (on this throne). Approaching that greatly intelligent (king), Shakuni thus spoke to him.

verses.sanskrit: प्रियकृन्मतमाज्ञाय पूर्वं दुर्योधनस्य तत्। प्रज्ञाचक्षुषमासीनं शकुनिः सौबलस्तदा॥२॥
verses.bhavadeepa: अनुभूयेति ॥१॥

verses.sanskrit: दुर्योधनवचः श्रुत्वा धृतराष्ट्रं जनाधिपम्। उपगम्य महाप्राज्ञं शकुनिर्वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥३॥
शकुनिरुवाच। दुर्योधनो महाराज विवर्णो हरिणः कृशः। दीनश्चिन्तापरश्चैव तं विद्धि मनुजाधिप॥४॥
verses.english: Shakuni said O great king, O best of the Bharata race, know that Duryodhana has become colourless, pale, and emaciated with anxiety. came

verses.sanskrit: न वै परीक्षसे सम्यगसह्यं शत्रुसंभवम्। ज्येष्ठपुत्रस्य हृच्छोकं किमर्थं नावबुध्यसे॥५॥
verses.english: Why do you not after due enquiry ascertain the cause of the grief that is in the heart of your eldest son, the grief caused by the enemy?
verses.bhavadeepa: विवर्णः पूर्ववर्णात् हीनवर्णः हरिणः पाण्डुः दीनः क्षीणदर्पः ॥४॥

verses.sanskrit:
धृतराष्ट्र उवाच।
              दुर्योधन कुतोमूलं भृशमार्तोऽसि पुत्रक। श्रोतव्यश्चेन्मया सोऽर्थो ब्रूहि मे कुरुनन्दन॥६॥
verses.english: Dhritarashtra said O Duryodhana, O son, what is the cause of your grief? O Kuru prince, if it is fit for me to hear, tell it to me.

verses.sanskrit: अयं त्वां शकुनिः प्राह विवर्णं हरिणं कृशम्। चिन्तयंश्च न पश्यामि शोकस्य तव सम्भवम्॥७॥
verses.english: This Shakuni says you are colourless, pale and emaciated. After reflection I can not find any cause for your grief.
verses.bhavadeepa: कुतोमूलं किंमूलं कुत इति प्रथमार्थे तसिः ॥६॥

verses.sanskrit: ऐश्वर्यं हि महत्पुत्र त्वयि सर्वं प्रतिष्ठितम्। भ्रातरः सुहृदश्चैव नाचरन्ति तवाप्रियम्॥८॥
verses.english: O son, all my vast wealth is at your command. Your brothers and our relatives and friends never do anything injurious to you.

verses.sanskrit: आच्छादयसि प्रावारानश्नासि पिशितौदनम्। आजानेया वहन्त्यश्वाः केनासि हरिणः कृशः॥९॥
verses.english: You wear the best robes, you eat food prepared with meat, you ride the best horses, why then are you pale and emaciated?

verses.sanskrit: शयनानि महार्हाणि योषितश्च मनोरमाः। गुणवन्ति च वेश्मानि विहाराश्च यथासुखम्॥१०॥
verses.english: Costly beds, the charming damsels finely furnished mansions and grounds of sport are at pleasure (when you amuse).
verses.bhavadeepa: पिशितौदनं मांसमयमन्नम् । आजानेयाः जात्यश्वाः ॥९॥

verses.sanskrit: देवनामिव ते सर्वं वाचि बद्धं न संशयः। स दीन इव दुर्धर्ष कस्माच्छोचसि पुत्रक॥११॥
verses.english: All these certainly wait your command as do they in the case of the celestials. () invincible hero, O son, why do you grieve (then) like a destitute person?
verses.bhavadeepa: विहाराः क्रीडास्थानानि ॥१०॥

verses.sanskrit:
दुर्योधन उवाच।
              अश्नाम्याच्छादये चाहं यथा कुपुरुषस्तथा। अमर्षं धारये चोग्रं निनीषुः कालपर्ययम्॥१२॥
verses.english: Duryodhana said I, no doubt, eat and dress but I pass my time all the while like a wretch, for I am a prey to jealousy.
verses.bhavadeepa: वाचि बद्धं वाग्व्यापारमात्रसाध्यम् ॥११॥

verses.sanskrit: अमर्षणः स्वाः प्रकृतीरभिभूय परं स्थितः। क्लेशान्मुमुक्षुः परजान्स वै पुरुष उच्यते॥१३॥
verses.english: He is called a (true) man who lives after having vanquished his enemy in order to liberate his own subjects from the tyranny of that enemy.

verses.sanskrit: सन्तोषो वै श्रियं हन्ति ह्यभिमानं च भारत। अनुक्रोशभये चोभे यैर्वृतो नाश्नुते महत्॥१४॥
verses.english: O descendant of Bharata, contentment and pride destroy (one's) prosperity. Being engrossed with compassion and fear he can never rise.
verses.bhavadeepa: प्रकृतीः प्रजाः क्लेशात् मुमुक्षुर्मोचयितुमिच्छन्नेव पुरुष इत्युच्यते ॥१३॥

verses.sanskrit: न मां प्रीणाति मद्भुक्तं श्रियं दृष्ट्वा युधिष्ठेरे। अतिज्वलन्तीं कौन्तेये विवर्णकरणीं मम॥१५॥
verses.english: Seeing the prosperity of Yudhishthira, whatever I enjoy does not gratify or please me. The great and splendid prosperity of the son of Kunti makes me pale.
verses.bhavadeepa: त्वत्प्रकृतयो निष्क्लेशा एव सन्तीत्यत आह यतः संतोषः ऐश्वर्यम् बलं बुद्धिः श्रियं विद्यमानामपि हन्तीति संतुष्टस्य प्रजाः क्लेशं प्राप्नुवन्त्येवेत्यर्थः । अभिमानं गर्वम् । अनुक्रोशो दया भयं स्वोच्छेददृष्टिः महत् । पदमिति शेषः ॥१४॥

verses.sanskrit: सपत्नानृध्यतोत्मानं हीयमानं निशम्य च। अदृश्यामपि कौन्तेयश्रियं पश्यन्निवोद्यताम्॥१६॥
verses.english: Though I am not now seeing the greatly effulgent prosperity of the son of Kunti, yet knowing the affluence of the foe and my destitution, I (feel as if I) see it before me. For this reason I am colourless melancholy, pale and emaciated.

verses.sanskrit: तस्मादहं विवर्णश्च दीनश्च हरिणः कृशः। अष्टाशीतिसहस्राणि स्नातका गृहमेधिनः॥१७॥
verses.english: Yudhishthira supports by giving thirty servant maids to each of eighty eight thousands Snataka Brahmanas who lead domestic life.
verses.bhavadeepa: ऋद्ध्यतः वर्द्धमानान् । आत्मानमिति छेदः पूर्वरूपमार्षम् । निशम्य विज्ञाय अदृश्यामपि व्यवहितत्वात् । कौन्तेयश्रियं मनसा उद्यतां पश्यन्निव विवर्णोऽस्मीत्यर्थः ॥१६॥

verses.sanskrit: त्रिंशद्दासीक एकैको यान्बिभर्ति युधिष्ठिरः। दशान्यानि सहस्राणि नित्यं तत्रान्नमुत्तमम्। भुञ्जते रुक्मपात्रीभिर्युधिष्ठिरनिवेशने॥१८॥
verses.english: Besides these, ten thousand other B:ahmanas daily eat well cooked food from golden plates at the palace of Yudhishthira.

verses.sanskrit: कदलीमृगमोकानि कृष्णश्यामारुणानि च। काम्भोजः प्राहिणोत्तस्मै परार्ध्यानपि कम्बलान्। गजयोषिद्गवाश्वस्य शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः॥१९॥
verses.english: The king of Kamboja sent to him hundreds and thousands of black darkish and red skins of the deer called Kadali, and also blankets of excellent texture. Hundreds and hundreds and thousands and thousands of female elephants, horses and cows and thirty thousand female camels wander (within his palace); the kings brought them all as tribute when they assembled there.

verses.sanskrit: त्रिशतं चोष्ट्रवामीनां शतानि विचरन्त्युत। राजन्या बलिमादाय समेता हि नृपक्षये॥२०॥
verses.bhavadeepa: कदलीमृगा हरिणविशेषास्तेषामोकानि अजिनानि तान्येव कृष्णश्यामारुणानि चित्रवर्णानीत्यर्थः ॥१९॥

verses.sanskrit: पृथग्विधानि रत्नानि पार्थिवाः पृथिवीपते। आहरन्क्रतुमुख्येऽस्मिन्कुन्तीपुत्राय भूरिशः॥२१॥
verses.english: O lord of earth, the kings brought to that foremost of sacrifice heaps of gems and jewels for the son of Kunti,

verses.sanskrit: न क्वचिद्धि मया तादृग्दृष्टपूर्वो न च श्रुतः। यादृग्धनागमो यज्ञे पाण्डुपुत्रस्य धीमतः॥२२॥
verses.english: I never heard or saw such enormous wealth as was brought to the sacrifice of the intelligent (son) of Pandu (Yudhishthira).

verses.sanskrit: अपर्यन्तं धनौघं तं दृष्ट्वा शत्रोरहं नृप। शमं नैवाभिगच्छामि चिन्तयानो विशाम्पते॥२३॥
verses.english: O king, seeing that enormous collection of wealth belonging to the enemy. I cannot enjoy peace of mind. 'I am afflicted with their thoughts. O king.

verses.sanskrit: ब्रह्मणा वाटधानाश्च गोमन्तः शतसङ्घशः। त्रिखर्वं बलिमादाय द्वारि तिष्ठन्ति वारिताः॥२४॥
verses.english: Being stopped there by the gatekeepers hundreds of Brahmanas, supported by the land presented to them (by Yudhishthira) and possessing wealth of kine, waited at the palace gate with three thousands of millions of tribute.

verses.sanskrit: कमण्डलूनुपादाय जातरूपमयाञ्शुभान्। एतद्धनं समादाय प्रवेशं लेभिरे न च॥२५॥
verses.english: Even having brought with them Ghee in golden Kamandalus (sort of water pot), they could not get admission into the palace.
verses.bhavadeepa: वाटाः क्षेत्रादिवृत्तयः तासां धाना अभिनवोद्भेदो येषां ते इति व्यधिकरणो बहुव्रीहिः सस्यादिसंपन्नक्षेत्रादिवृत्तिमन्त इत्यर्थः । ‘वाटो वृत्तौ च गाय च’ इति । ‘धाना भ्रष्टयवे प्रोक्ता धान्याकेभिनवोद्भदि’ इति विश्वः । त्रिखर्वं खर्वत्रयसङ्ख्यम् ॥२४॥

verses.sanskrit: यथैव मधु शक्राय धारयन्त्यमरस्त्रियः। तदस्मै कांस्यमाहार्षीद्वारुणं कलशोदधिः॥२६॥
verses.english: Ocean himself brought to him in vessels of white copper Ambrosia which was generated within his waters and which was superior to that which the wives of the immortal (Soma, i.e. flowers and annual plants) produce for Shakra (Indra)
verses.bhavadeepa: कमण्डलूनिति । ‘इन्द्रियं वा एतदस्मिल्लोके यद्दधि’ इति खण्डे बह्वृचब्राह्मणे दधिमधुघृतम् आपश्चेत्यभिषेकद्रव्याणि विहितानि । तत्रेतरेषामग्रे दर्शनात् इह कमण्डलून् घृतपूर्णानिति द्रष्टव्यम् ॥२५॥

verses.sanskrit: शङ्खप्रवरमादाय वासुदेवोऽभिषिक्तवान्। शक्यं रुक्मसहस्रस्य बहुरत्नविभूषितम्॥२७॥
verses.english: Having brought an excellent conch, Vasudeva bathed him (Yudhishthira at the conclusion of the sacrifice) with they holy water brought in one thousand golden jars inlaid with numerous gems.
verses.bhavadeepa: यथैवेति अमरः सोमः तस्य स्त्रिय ओषधयः । तद्दिव्यं मधु अस्मै कांस्यं कांस्यपात्रस्थं कृत्वा आहार्षीत् । अर्थात्सोम एव तथा वारुणं वरुणप्रेषितं दधि प्रसिद्धम् । कलश इव कलशो जलपूर्णत्वात्समुद्रः आहार्षीत् । दधिरिति पुंस्त्वम् आर्षं लेखकप्रमादो वा । अन्ये तु कलशोदधिः समुद्रः मधु अमृतं जलमित्यन्ये अमरस्त्रियो नद्यः वारुणं वरुणसंबन्धीति व्याचक्षते ॥२६॥

verses.sanskrit: दृष्ट्वा च मम तत्सर्वं ज्वररूपमिवाभवत्। गृहीत्वा तत्तु गच्छन्ति समुद्रौ पूर्वदक्षिणौ॥२८॥
verses.bhavadeepa: शैक्यं वरत्रामयं पात्राधारभूतं शिक्यं ‘कावडी’ इति प्रसिद्धम् । तत्र स्थितं पात्रं शक्यम् । एतेन सामुद्र्य आप उक्ताः अन्या अपि पुण्या आपोऽभिषेकार्थमुक्ताः प्रदेशान्तरे । ‘वापीकूपतटाकेभ्यो ह्रदेभ्यः सरसस्तथा । चतुर्भ्यश्च समुद्रेभ्यः पल्वलादभिसंधितः ॥ प्रयागाद्देवयजनाज्जलान्यादाय सर्वतः । गङ्गा सरस्वती चैव नर्मदा च दृषद्वतीद्गती ॥ एभ्यो जलं समादाय तत्राभिषिषिचुर्द्विजाः’ इति ॥२७॥

verses.sanskrit: तथैव पश्चिमं यान्ति गृहीत्वा भरतर्षभ। उत्तरं तु न गच्छन्ति विना तात पतत्रिणः॥२९॥
तत्र गत्वाऽर्जुनो दण्डमाजहारामितं धनम्। इदं चाद्भुतमत्रासीत्तन्मे निगदतः शृणु॥३०॥
verses.english: Arjuna, however, went there and exacted as tribute a vast quantity of wealth. There happened another wonderful incident, which I shall describe to you. Listen to it.
verses.bhavadeepa: पतत्रिणः खेचरजातीयाः तैरेवोत्तरसमुद्रजलमानीतमित्यर्थः । अन्यथा चतुर्भ्यश्च समुद्रेभ्य इत्यनुपपन्नं स्यात् ॥२९॥

verses.sanskrit: पूर्णे शतसहस्रे तु विप्राणां परिविष्यताम्। स्थापिता तत्र सञ्ज्ञाभूच्छङ्खो ध्मायति नित्यशः॥३१॥
verses.english: When (full) one lac Brahmanas were every day fed, it was arranged (to notify) the fact by blowing conchs in a chorus.

verses.sanskrit: मुहुर्मुहुः प्रणदतस्तस्य शङ्खस्य भारत। अनिशं शब्दमश्रौषं ततो रोमाणि मेऽहृषन्॥३२॥
verses.english: O descendant of Bharata, I continually heard (choruses of) conchs blown; and that too often repeatedly. It each time indicated that one lac Brahmanas had been fed. Having heard these sounds, my hairs stood on end.
verses.bhavadeepa: परिविष्यतां परिवेष्यमाणानां संज्ञा सङ्केतः ॥३१॥

verses.sanskrit: पार्थिवैर्बहुभिः कीर्णमुपस्थानं दिदृक्षुभिः। अशोभत महाराज नक्षत्रैर्द्यैरिवामला॥३३॥
verses.english: O great king, that palatial grounds crowded with many kings who came there as spectators, looked as beautiful as the cloudless sky studded with stars.

verses.sanskrit: सर्वरत्नान्युपादाय पार्थिवा वै जनेश्वर। यज्ञे तस्य महाराज पाण्डुपुत्रस्य धीमतः॥३४॥
verses.english: O ruler of men, O great king, the monarchs came to the sacrifice of the wise son of Pandu, bringing with them every king of wealth.
verses.bhavadeepa: उपतिष्ठन्त्यस्मिन्नित्युपस्थानं सभाम् ॥३३॥

verses.sanskrit: वैश्या इव महीपाला द्विजातिपरिवेषकाः। न सा श्रीर्देवराजस्य यमस्य वरुणस्य च। गुह्यकाधिपतेर्वापि या श्री राजन्युधिष्ठिरे॥३५॥
verses.english: Like the Vaishyas the kings became the distributors of food to the Brahmanas. Such wealth does not belong even to the king of the celestials (Indra) or to Yama or to Varuna,
verses.bhavadeepa: उपादाय स्थिता इति शेषः ॥३४॥

verses.sanskrit: तां दृष्ट्वा पाण्डुपुत्रस्य श्रियं परमिक्रामहम्। शान्तिं न परिगच्छामि दह्यमानेन चेतसा॥३६॥
verses.english: Or to the lord of the Guhyakas, as belongs to Yudhishthira. O king, seeing that great prosperity of the son of Pandu, my heart is burning. I cannot get peace (of mind).

verses.sanskrit: शकुनिरुवाच। यामेतामतुलां लक्ष्मीं दृष्टवानसि पाण्डवे। तस्याः प्राप्तावुपायं मे शृणु सत्यपराक्रम॥३७॥
verses.english: Shakuni said O hero whose prowess is truth, hear the means by which you can obtain the matchless prosperity that you have seen in the Pandava.

verses.sanskrit: अहमक्षेष्वभिज्ञातः पृथिव्यामपि भारत। हृदयज्ञः पणज्ञश्च विशेषज्ञश्च देवने॥३८॥
verses.english: O descendant of Bharata, I am an adept in dice, superior to all in the world. I can ascertain the success or otherwise of every throw, and also when to stake and when not to stake. I have special knowledge of the play.

verses.sanskrit: द्यूतप्रियश्च कौन्तेयो न च जानाति देवितुम्। आहूतश्चैष्यति व्यक्तं द्यूतादपि रणादपि॥३९॥
verses.english: The son of Kunti (Yudhishthira) is also fond of the play, although he possesses little skill in it. He is sure to come, if challenged to pay or to fight.
verses.bhavadeepa: अक्षेषु पाशेषु अभिज्ञातः कुशलः । हृदयज्ञः पातयिष्यमाणानामक्षाणां जयपराजयावहत्वाभिज्ञः पणज्ञः तदनुसारेण द्रव्यप्रयोगवित् । विशेषज्ञः दिक्कालाद्यानुकूल्याभिज्ञः ॥३८॥

verses.sanskrit: नियतं तं विजेष्यामि कृत्वा तु कपटं विभो। आनयामि समृद्धिं तां दिव्यां चोपाह्वयस्व तम्॥४०॥
verses.english: O lord, I shall always defeat him at every throw by practising deception. I shall win all.. his celestial-like wealth; and you will (then) be able to enjoy it.
verses.bhavadeepa: द्यूतात् द्यूतहेतोः रणात् रणहेतोः ॥३९॥

verses.sanskrit:
वैशम्पायन उवाच।
              एवमुक्तः शकुनिना राजा दुर्योधनस्ततः। धृतराष्ट्रमिदं वाक्यमपदान्तरमब्रवीत्॥४१॥
verses.english: Vaishampayana said Having been thus addressed by Shakuni, the king Duryodhana, without allowing a moment to elapse, spoke thus to Dhritarashtra.
verses.bhavadeepa: कपटम् अक्षाधिष्ठात्र्या देवताया वशीकरणम् । यद्वा सर्वतश्चतुष्कोणतया द्वादशधारेष्वक्षेषु षट्तलानि भवन्ति । येषु त्रिषु त्रिषु देवयित्रोर्नामनी लिख्येते । तत्र कपटम् अन्तः सुषिरमक्षं कृत्वा परनामाङ्कितप्रदेशं गर्भे गुरुद्रव्यसंश्लिष्टं कृत्वा पातितस्याक्षस्य स्वनामैवोपरिभवति तदा स्वस्य जयः परस्य नामाधस्थं तस्य पराजय इति ॥४०॥

verses.sanskrit: अयमुत्सहते राजन्श्रियमाहर्तुमक्षवित्। द्यूतेन पाण्डुपुत्रस्य तदनुज्ञातुमर्हसि॥४२॥
verses.english: O king, this (Shakuni) is an adept in dice; he is ready to win at dice the wealth of the sons of Pandu. You should grant him permission.

verses.sanskrit:
धृतराष्ट्र उवाच।
              क्षत्ता मन्त्री महाप्राज्ञः स्थितो यस्यास्मि शासने। तेन सङ्गम्य वेत्स्यामि कार्यस्यास्य विनिश्चयम्॥४३॥
verses.english: Dhritarashtra says I always follow the counsel of greatly intelligent Khattwa (Vidura), my minister. Having consulted with him, I shall inform you my decision (in this matter).
verses.bhavadeepa: अपदान्तरम् अनुपदमेव  ॥४२॥

verses.sanskrit: स हि धर्मं पुरस्कृत्य दीर्घदर्शी परं हितम्। उभयोः पक्षयोर्युक्तं वक्ष्यत्यर्थविनिश्चयम्॥४४॥
verses.english: He is endued with great foresight; keeping the rules of morality before his eyes, he will point out what is good and what is proper for both parties and what should be done in this matter.

verses.sanskrit:
दुर्योधन उवाच।
              निवर्तयिष्यति त्वाऽसौ यदि क्षत्ता समेष्यति। निवृत्ते त्वयि राजेन्द्र मरिष्येऽहमसंशयम्॥४५॥
verses.english: Duryodhana said If you consult with Kshatta (Vidura) he will make you desist (from it). O king of kings, if you desist (from this), I will certainly kill myself.

verses.sanskrit: स त्वं मयि मृते राजन्विदुरेण सुखी भव। भोक्ष्यसे पृथिवीं कृत्स्नां किं मया त्वं करिष्यसि॥४६॥
verses.english: O king, when I am dead, be happy with Vidura. Enjoy then the whole earth. What need you have with me?
verses.bhavadeepa: त्वासौ त्वा त्वाम् असौ निवर्तयिष्यति । त्वासावित्यादेर्विवर्णतां चैव सशोकतां चेत्यन्तस्य दुर्योधनविलापस्य तात्पर्यं पुण्यवतामीश्वरप्रसादलभ्यां वृद्धिं दृष्ट्वा पापिनां परितापो भवतीति ॥४५॥

verses.sanskrit:
शम्पायन उवाच।
              आर्तवाक्यं तु तत्तस्य प्रणयोक्तं निशम्य सः। धृतराष्ट्रोऽब्रवीत्प्रेष्यान्दुर्योधनमते स्थितः॥४७॥
verses.english: Vaishampayana said Hearing his (Duryodhana's) words of affection. Dhritarashtra, ever ready to do what Duryodhana said, commanded his servant thus.

verses.sanskrit: स्थूणासहस्रैर्बृहतीं शतद्वारां सभां मम। मनोरमां दर्शनीयामाशु कुर्वन्तुं शिल्पिनः॥४८॥
verses.english: Dhritarashtra said. Let artifices be employed to crect without delay a delightful, charming and spacious Sabha with one hundred doors and with one thousand pillars.

verses.sanskrit: ततः संस्तीर्य रत्नैस्तां तक्ष्ण आनाय्य सर्वशः। सुकृतां सुप्रवेशां च निवेदयत मे शनैः॥४९॥
verses.english: Having brought carpenters and joiners, set jewels and precious stones all over its walls. Make it handsome and easy of access; and then inform me when every thing is complete.

verses.sanskrit: दूर्योधनस्य शान्त्यर्थमिति निश्चित्य भूमिपः। धृतराष्ट्रो महाराज प्राहिणोद्विदुराय वै॥५०॥
verses.english: Vaishampayana said O great king, having resolved to pacify Duryodhana the ruler of earth, Dhritarashtra, sent men to Vidura to summon him (before his presence).
verses.bhavadeepa: रत्नैः संस्तीर्य रत्नखचितां कृत्वा । तक्ष्णः वर्धकिनः । सर्वशः सर्वदेशीयान् ॥४९॥

verses.sanskrit: अपृष्ट्वा विदुरं स्वस्य नासीत्कश्चिद्विनिश्चयः। द्यूते दोषांश्च जानन्स पुत्रस्नेहादकृष्यत॥५१॥
verses.english: Because without asking Vidura, he (Dhritarashtra) never framed any resolution. Knowing (full well) the evils of gambling, he was still attracted towards it out of his fondness for his son.

verses.sanskrit: तच्छ्रुत्वा विदुरो धीमान्कलिद्वारमुपस्थितम्। विनाशमुखमुत्पन्नं धृतराष्ट्रमुपाद्रवत्॥५२॥
verses.english: Having heard this, the intelligent Vidura knew that the arrival of Kali (Yuga) is near at hand. Seeing also the way to destruction (of the Kuru race) about to the opened, he soon came to Dhritarashtra.

verses.sanskrit: सोऽभिगम्य महात्मानं भ्राता भ्रातरमग्रजम्। मूर्ध्ना प्रणम्य चरणाविदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥५३॥
verses.english: Coming to his illustrious eldest brother and bowing his head to his feet, he thus spoke to him.

verses.sanskrit:
विदुर उवाच।
              नाभिनन्दामि ते राजन्व्यवसायमिमं प्रभो। पुत्रैर्भेदो यथा न स्थाद्द्यूतहेतोस्तथा कुरु॥५४॥
verses.english: Vidura said O king, O lord, I do not approve of the resolution you have formed. You should act in such a way that no dispute may arise amongst your sons on account of this gambling.

verses.sanskrit:
धृतराष्ट्र उवाच।
              क्षत्तः पुत्रेषु पुत्रैर्मे कलहो न भविष्यति। यदि देवाः प्रसादं नः करिष्यन्ति न संशयः॥५५॥
verses.english: Dhritarashtra said O Khattwa, there is no doubt that if the gods are propitious to us, no dispute will ever arise amongst my children.
verses.bhavadeepa: व्यवसायं विनिश्चयम् ॥५४॥

verses.sanskrit: अशुभं वा शुभं वापि हितं वा यदि वाऽहितम्। प्रवर्ततां सुहृद्द्यूतं दिष्टमेतन्न संशयः॥५६॥
verses.english: Auspicious or not auspicious, beneficial or not beneficial, let this friendly gambling match be held. This is certainly what Fate has ordained (for us).

verses.sanskrit: मयि सन्निहिते द्रोणे भीष्मे त्वयि च भारत। अनयो दैवविहितो न कथञ्चिद्भविष्यति॥५७॥
verses.english: O descendant of Bharata, when Drona, Bhishma, you and I will be near at hand, no evil, can possible happen, even if Fate has ordained it.
verses.bhavadeepa: दिष्टं दैवम् ॥५६॥

verses.sanskrit: गच्छ त्वं रथमास्थाय हयैर्वातसमैर्जवे। खाण्डवप्रस्थमद्यैव समानय युधिष्ठिरम्॥५८॥
verses.english: Go ascending a car yoked with horses possessing the speed of wind, so that you may reach Khandavaprastha day. Bring Yudhishthira with you.

verses.sanskrit: न वाच्यो व्यवसायो मे विदुरैतद्ब्रवीमि ते। दैवमेव परं मन्ये येनैतदुपपद्यते॥५९॥
verses.english: O Vidura, I tell you, this is my resolution. Do not tell me any thing. I regard Fate as supreme; she brings all this.

verses.sanskrit: इत्युक्तो विदुरो धीमान्नेदमस्तीति चिन्तयन्। आपगेयं महाप्राज्ञमभ्यगच्छत्सुदुःखितः॥६०॥
verses.english: Vaishampayana said Having heard this, and having concluded that his race was doomed, the intelligent to Vidura went to the greatly wise Bhishma in great sorrow.
